item.title: Trump aims to leave a physical legacy in D.C., bulldozing norms along the way
item.description: President Trump has brought his New York real estate background to the White House. But experts say D.C. is a very different historic and legal landscape — and worry about the precedent he could set.
item.content:encoded: President Trump has brought his New York real estate background to the White House. But experts say D.C. is a very different historic and legal landscape — and worry about the precedent he could set.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Treisman

item.title: Welcome to the 'Wild West' of AI in schools: Research is scarce, but experiments abound
item.description: Teachers are using AI to develop lesson plans, and in some districts, AI chatbots give students feedback on their work. Meanwhile, the research around how AI can help students is extremely limited.
item.content:encoded: Teachers are using AI to develop lesson plans, and in some districts, AI chatbots give students feedback on their work. Meanwhile, the research around how AI can help students is extremely limited.
item.dc:creator: Lee V. Gaines

item.title: How to limit the rat numbers? Train the humans
item.description: D.C.'s Rat Rangers take anyone who is interested on night time safaris through some of the Capitol's filthiest back alleys to learn the way of the rats, and to be better humans.

item.title: Nor'easter wallops Northeast coastal communities
item.description: Northeast coastal communities are assessing damage from an early-season nor'easter that brought high winds and lashing rain, coinciding with high tides from Virginia to southern Maine.

item.title: California health officials warn of possible measles exposure in 6 counties
item.description: California health officials are on the lookout for new measles cases, after someone with the vaccine-preventable disease rode a passenger train and busses through six counties.

item.title: Fall planting isn't over. Try greens, garlic or both
item.description: A University of Maryland farm manager explains why Swiss chard and garlic are good choices for a home garden this fall.

item.title: The L.A. fires gave new life to a composer's firefighter anthem
item.description: LA-based composer Charles-Henri Avelange wrote a score to honor firefighters almost 20 years ago. After last year's wildfires in Los Angeles, he's made headway in finally recording it.

item.title: Maricopa County official on how they're tackling mistrust around election security
item.description: As President Trump questions election security, many local officials are trying to reassure voters. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Kate Brophy McGee, chair of the Maricopa County Board of Supervisors.

item.title: As Congress debates college sports, athletes-turned-senators have a seat at the table
item.description: The Protect College Sports Act is on the brink of passing in the Senate, where a handful of former college athletes who are now senators on both sides of the aisle have an extra say in the debate.

item.title: After Hurricane Helene, this community was inspired to learn how to use power tools
item.description: People in western North Carolina are learning to use power tools two years after Hurricane Helene. They want to be prepared for future disasters.
